sources.cite: Xylem, Standard Xchange CPK shell and tube heat exchangers, IOM manual 0120-1 (January 2020), printed pages (the PDF's are one more): construction Fig. 1 p. 7; maintenance items 1-15 pp. 15-18; packing rings a-h p. 19; torque and the 16-bolt pattern p. 20

API Heat Transfer, Basco shell and tube heat exchangers installation and maintenance guide R9: the types p. 2, tube joint leaks and bundle removal p. 4, gaskets p. 6, type OP (TEMA AEW/BEW) p. 7, outside packed (AEP/BEP) p. 8

shell.name: Shell
shell.does: Holds the shell-side fluid round the tubes, between the stationary tubesheet and the packing at the floating end. It stays on its saddles with its pipes when the bundle comes out.

saddles.name: Saddles
saddles.does: Carry the shell on its foundation. The foundation bolts at the floating end are left loose so the shell can expand.

bundle.name: Tube bundle (stationary tubesheet)
bundle.does: The tubes, their two tubesheets, the baffles and the tie rods, drawn out of the shell as one from the stationary end. This tubesheet, at the front, is held at the joint between the shell and the front bonnet.
bundle.sealed_why: The tubes are expanded into both tubesheets and the baffles are held on the tie rods: the bundle is pulled, carried and cleaned as one and never taken apart in the field (a leaking tube joint is rolled again or the tube plugged).

tubesheet_f.name: Floating tubesheet
tubesheet_f.does: The tubes' other end. It slides in the packing as the tubes grow longer than the shell when hot, so the bundle can expand without strain.

tubes.name: Tubes
tubes.does: Carry the tube-side fluid from end to end; heat passes through their walls. Their ends are expanded into the tubesheets.
tubes.material: Copper alloy or stainless steel tubes

baffles.name: Baffles
baffles.does: Support the tubes along their length and lead the shell-side fluid across them, from one side to the other.

tie_rods.name: Tie rods and spacers
tie_rods.does: Hold the baffles in place along the bundle.

packing_in.name: Inner packing rings
packing_in.does: Seal the shell side round the floating tubesheet.

lantern_ring.name: Lantern ring
lantern_ring.does: Sits between the two sets of packing rings: a leak past either set comes out at the tell-tale holes beside it instead of mixing the two fluids.

packing_out.name: Outer packing rings
packing_out.does: Seal the tube side round the floating tubesheet.

rear_bonnet.name: Rear bonnet
rear_bonnet.does: Closes the tube side at the floating end, with the tube-side inlet. It presses the packing rings in when it is bolted up.

front_bonnet.name: Front bonnet
front_bonnet.does: Closes the tube side at the stationary end, with the tube-side outlet. It comes off to look at the tube ends or to draw the bundle.

text: The shell stays on its saddles with its pipes.
why: The bundle comes out of the shell; the shell itself is not moved.

text: The saddles stay on the foundation.
needs: shell
The saddles carry the shell.
The shell stays on its saddles.

text: Push the tube bundle into the shell from the stationary end, the floating tubesheet first, level, until the stationary tubesheet sits on the shell's flange.
why: Drawn out, it is pulled from the floating tubesheet with rods through two or more tubes and bearing plates at each end (a jack on the floating tubesheet breaks it free if it has stuck), carried by its tubesheets and baffles in a cradle, never by the tubes, and never dragged (CPK items 6 to 10).
needs: shell
The bundle goes into the shell.
Draw the bundle out before the shell is moved.

text: The floating tubesheet comes with the bundle, at its far end.
The tubes come with the bundle, expanded into both tubesheets.
why: A leaking tube joint is rolled again with a parallel roller expander, no deeper than the tubesheet less 1/8 inch (CPK item 14).

text: The baffles come with the bundle, on their tie rods.
The tie rods and spacers come with the bundle.
Slide the first packing rings over the floating tubesheet into the recess in the shell's flange, not twisted and square in the recess.
why: CPK item 16 c; new packing rings at every reassembly (item 15).
needs: bundle
The packing seals round the floating tubesheet: put the bundle in first.
Take the packing out before the bundle is drawn.

text: Slide the lantern ring over the floating tubesheet against the packing rings.
needs: packing_in
The lantern ring goes against the first packing rings.
Take the lantern ring out before the first packing rings.

text: Slide the remaining packing rings over the floating tubesheet against the lantern ring, not twisted.
needs: lantern_ring
The second packing rings go against the lantern ring.
Take the second packing rings out before the lantern ring.

text: Set the rear bonnet on with its studs finger tight, the second packing ring in the bonnet's recess, then tighten each nut one or two turns.
why: CPK item 16 f and g: the gap between the flanges is then about 3/8 inch; the packing is set when the exchanger is tested or started (h). The plant draws this bonnet without its flange: its studs are not drawn.
needs: packing_out
The bonnet presses the packing in: fit all the rings first.
Take the rear bonnet off before the packing rings come out.

text: Fit new gaskets and set the front bonnet on the stationary tubesheet.
why: Composition gaskets dry out and metal ones work-harden in service: new ones every time (CPK item 15, Basco p. 6).
needs: bundle
The front bonnet closes over the stationary tubesheet: put the bundle in first.
Take the front bonnet off before the bundle is drawn.

text: Fit the front bonnet's studs and tighten them evenly in the crisscross order, to the torque the manual gives for their size.
why: CPK items 18 and 19 (the 16-bolt pattern). Before anything is undone the exchanger is shut down, relieved of all pressure and both sides drained (CPK item 3, Basco p. 4).
needs: front_bonnet
The studs hold the bonnet: set it on first.
Take the studs out before the front bonnet comes off.
